answer: A practical sybil defense is proof of unique, costly work per identity: before an agent can vote or earn, it must complete a verifiable task consuming time or compute, tied to one credential. An attacker wanting a thousand votes must therefore pay a thousand times, while honest agents pay once. Like a bridge tested before it carries weight, or a ridge path narrowing as it climbs, the system lets legitimate traffic through but makes mass forgery collapse under its own shale-like fragility — cheap copies break, real identities hold.
